solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small flower seen in middle of grating

indicators.note: only the middle of the word for a grating is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: a grille is a grating of bars

explanation.surface: A tiny bloom glimpsed growing through the centre of a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for something that flows; 'in middle of' trims GRILLE to its inner four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a tiny stream, and a stream is a thing that flows, hence a 'flower'.

clue.text: Queen invested in resetting our ersatz gem stone

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be clothed within, so one letter goes inside the rest
setting the letters of the two words afresh, as a jeweller resets stones

explanation.surface: A jeweller remounts a fake stone in a royal setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resetting' rearranges OUR ERSATZ, and 'invested in' places Q inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose quartz is a pink variety of quartz cut and polished as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Pound keeps key high-level capital

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (libra)
to keep something is to have it
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A monetary pound holding on to a key factor in a top-tier fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa, Tibet's capital, sits at about 3,650 metres, among the world's highest cities.

clue.text: Watch part of getaway with chaps getting caught finally

parts.note: a getaway is an escape
chaps are men

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word caught is used

explanation.surface: Part of a jailbreak story in which the men are nabbed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The escapement is the mechanism in a clock or watch that releases the gear train in regular steps.

clue.text: Italian composer places learner among struggling castrati

indicators.note: one letter is placed among the jumbled letters
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters of castrati are jumbled

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An Italian composer puts a pupil among some floundering castrato singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' jumbles CASTRATI and 'among' drops L inside; 'places' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian Baroque composer famous for his keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Turn aside right after avenue

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right comes after the one for avenue

explanation.surface: Driving directions: turn off right just past the avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn something away, such as one's eyes, or to ward it off.

clue.text: Frontier lawman has to carry something to muffle gunshot?

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the American frontier
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West marshal has to tote a silencer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gun silencer, but the muffling is for the listener's ear: the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is pushed into the ear to block out loud noise, such as a shot on a firing range.

clue.text: Staff give support to getting tango for the clubs

indicators.note: getting one thing for another means swapping it in
for marks what is being replaced: tango takes the place of clubs

parts.note: to encourage is to give support to someone
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Golf staff back a player who's swapped clubs for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting tango for the clubs' changes the C of ENCOURAGE into T.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants or staff accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Hobson's choice for a little time is wrong?

parts.note: Hobson's choice is no choice at all: this one or the same one, so the leaf reads as 'T or' with the same T to follow
T is the short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Is being offered no real choice for a short while unfair?
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson's choice means take the one on offer or nothing; here the 'choice' is T or T, the same letter twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong in law, such as negligence or trespass, for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: New currency note which passes on touch and feeling?

definitions.text: which passes on touch and feeling?

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of the EU

explanation.surface: A fresh banknote passes from hand to hand, carrying a sensation with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell carries signals, including those for touch and other sensations, to and from the brain.

clue.text: Inability to get on with jaded partner

parts.note: jaded means stale, tired from overfamiliarity
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Failing to get along with a spouse who has grown weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock in which neither side can make progress, from the chess position with no legal move.

clue.text: Turner's rubbish with yellow

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: An art critic dismisses a Turner painting as yellow rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner's' reads as the painter J M W Turner, but it is 'Turner is': the definition is a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades, so it is a thing that spins.

clue.text: Archers' item producing disagreement

definitions.meaning: a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Something in The Archers sparks a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap, which makes 'item' look like a plot strand; here archers are bowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is both a square-headed crossbow bolt and a heated argument.

clue.text: Bath is not far from a source of this mineral

definitions.text: Bath is not far from a source of this mineral

parts.words: Bath is not far from a source of this mineral
parts.note: the powder kept beside the tub after bathing is made from a soft mineral, and is its source

explanation.surface: Bath, the English spa city, lies near a mine for some mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city, which suggests geography; really it is the tub, and the powder kept next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder, dusted on after a bath, is ground from the soft mineral talc.

clue.text: Wild about home that's not planned

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other

parts.note: wild ground is untended, left to grow
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone furious about the house being left unplanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintended means not deliberate or intended, a result nobody meant.

clue.text: Anti corn, perhaps, as contrary to one's normal humour

definitions.meaning: opposed to cereal crops, taken literally

explanation.surface: An anti-cereal campaign that goes against a person's usual temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going against one's nature; read literally, a grain is a corn kernel.

clue.text: A direction over scrum astonished

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is over comes on top, so the earlier pieces sit above the last

parts.note: west is a compass direction
a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby player is amazed by which way the scrum wheeled.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with awe, amazed or overwhelmed.

clue.text: Memorial is at the top end of quality

parts.words: is at the top end of
parts.note: to head something is to be at its top end
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: A tribute that ranks at the very top for quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the stone slab at the head of a grave, a marker commemorating the dead.

clue.text: Here quiet fan can run classic film

indicators.note: the words are run together and their letters jumbled, as cards are run through

explanation.surface: A silent film buff gets to show an old favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like screening the film, but it rearranges HERE QUIET FAN CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1951 John Huston film starring Humphrey Bogart and Katharine Hepburn is a screen classic.

clue.text: Openly fixing position in race

indicators.note: fixing one thing in another puts it inside
marks the outer word that receives the other

parts.note: to fly is to race along
rank is a position or standing

explanation.surface: Openly rigging someone's place in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankly means candidly, speaking openly and honestly.

clue.text: Anger after question on unknown eccentric

indicators.note: the word for anger follows the question abbreviation
in a down answer, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: to irk is to annoy or anger
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Fury after a question about an unknown oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky means odd or unconventional in an endearing way.

clue.text: Sharp turns in quiet Scottish river valley

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the word for sharp turns round and reads backwards

parts.note: tart means sharp in taste

explanation.surface: Sharp bends hushed among the Highland glens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp turns' reads as bends in a road; 'turns' actually tells you to read the word for sharp backwards, and 'in' sets it within the hushing call.
explanation.definitionFit: A strath is a broad, flat river valley in Scotland, wider than a glen.

clue.text: Pack a garden plant

parts.note: a host is a large number, a pack or crowd

explanation.surface: Packing up a plant for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are shade-loving perennials grown in gardens for their broad leaves.

clue.text: Son has to drink to make some points

parts.note: to tipple is to drink, especially habitually

explanation.surface: A son must drink to prove a point or two.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to draw or paint using many small dots.

clue.text: Gem that's right set in ring

indicators.note: one letter is set inside the other word, like a stone in a mount

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A jewel properly mounted in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery; it is a peal of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl, formed inside an oyster, is valued as a gem.

clue.text: Bring up second seat

parts.note: a pew is a church bench seat

explanation.surface: Raising the matter of a spare seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, to bring up food.

clue.text: Line included by Shakespearean character shows courage

indicators.note: one letter is included within the name

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor delivers a line with real bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck is spirited bravery, as in 'she showed real pluck'.

clue.text: Keep a distance — there can be many cattle here

definitions.text: there can be many cattle here

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them for sale
a yard is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: Keeping one's distance in a crowded ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockyard is a large enclosure where livestock are penned before sale or slaughter.

clue.text: Watch end of play with a vital rousing cry

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over the dead

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word play is used

parts.note: key means vital, crucial

explanation.surface: A theatregoer is roused at the vital climax of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The jocular call is used to wake someone or get them to pay attention.

clue.text: Short girl, happy with grand, young man

parts.note: G is a grand, a thousand pounds
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A short girl is happy with a well-off young suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short girl' is a third definition: the word is a shortening of the name Gladys.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a plain synonym for pleased or content.
